import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Calculate effect sizes and p-values for all features
    effect_sizes = []
    p_values = []
    
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        col = feats.column(fid)
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, col]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, col]
        mean_diff = np.mean(y1) - np.mean(y0)
        t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(y1, y0, equal_var=False)
        effect_sizes.append(abs(mean_diff))
        p_values.append(p_val)
    
    # Rank features by effect size
    ranked_indices = np.argsort(effect_sizes)[::-1]
    
    # Select top candidates, avoiding near-duplicates
    selected_features = []
    excluded = set()
    
    # Check correlations to identify near-duplicates
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    n_features = len(feats.ids)
    
    for i in range(min(10, len(feats.ids))):  # Top 10 features
        idx = ranked_indices[i]
        fid = feats.ids[idx]
        
        # Skip if highly correlated with already selected features
        is_duplicate = False
        for selected_fid in selected_features:
            j = feats.column(selected_fid)
            corr = abs(corr_matrix[idx, j])
            if corr >= 0.6:
                is_duplicate = True
                break
        
        if not is_duplicate:
            selected_features.append(fid)
            if len(selected_features) >= MAX_DRIVERS:
                break
    
    # If no strong signals, return empty design
    if not selected_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Build regression components
    columns = tuple(selected_features)
    
    # Add interaction terms for top features (limit to 3 features max)
    products = []
    for i, a in enumerate(columns[:3]):
        for b in columns[i+1:]:
            products.append((a, b))
    
    # Create weighted score from top features
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(columns[:3]):
        col = feats.column(fid)
        # Weight by effect size (more important features get higher weights)
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, col]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, col]
        effect_size = abs(np.mean(y1) - np.mean(y0))
        loadings[fid] = effect_size
    
    # Limit total terms to avoid overfitting
    if len(columns) + len(products) > 12:
        # Keep only top 3 features and their interactions
        columns = columns[:3]
        products = [(a, b) for a, b in products if a in columns and b in columns]
    
    return Design(drivers=columns[:1], columns=columns, products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
